# dgtsv

> Solves a general real tridiagonal system of linear equations A * X = B.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dgtsv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dgtsv';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dgtsv( order, N, nrhs, DL, strideDL, d, strideD, DU, strideDU, B, LDB ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The order of the matrix A.<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B.<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `DL` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, DL must contain the (n-1) sub-diagonal elements of A. On exit, DL is overwritten by the (n-2) elements of the second super-diagonal of the upper triangular matrix U from the LU factorization of A, in DL(1), ..., DL(n-2). |
| ↳ `strideDL` | `integer` | Stride length for `DL` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, D must contain the diagonal elements of A. On exit, D is overwritten by the n diagonal elements of U. |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| `DU` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, DU must contain the (n-1) super-diagonal elements of A. On exit, DU is overwritten by the (n-1) elements of the first super-diagonal of U. |
| ↳ `strideDU` | `integer` | Stride length for `DU` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, the N by NRHS matrix of right hand side matrix B. On exit, if INFO = 0, the N by NRHS solution matrix X. |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `B`<br>Column-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, N)`<br>Row-major requires `LDB ≥ max(1, nrhs)` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `DL`: On entry, `DL` must contain the (n-1) sub-diagonal elements of A.

  On exit, `DL` is overwritten by the (n-2) elements of the second super-diagonal of the upper triangular matrix U from the LU factorization of A, in `DL(1)`, ..., `DL(n-2)`.
- `d`: On entry, D must contain the diagonal elements of A.

  On exit, D is overwritten by the n diagonal elements of U.
- `DU`: On entry, `DU` must contain the (n-1) super-diagonal elements of A.

  On exit, `DU` is overwritten by the (n-1) elements of the first super-diagonal of U.
- `B`: On entry, the N by `NRHS` matrix of right hand side matrix B. On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the N by `NRHS` solution matrix X.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dgtsv.ndarray(
    N, nrhs,
    DL, strideDL, offsetDL,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    DU, strideDU, offsetDU,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB
) → integer
```

Solves a general real tridiagonal system of linear equations A * X = B.
using Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix A<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of right hand sides<br>Requires `nrhs ≥ 0` |
| `DL` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | **in/out** · Sub-diagonal elements (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDL` | `integer` | Stride length for `DL` |
| ↳ `offsetDL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `DL` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Diagonal elements (length N) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `d` |
| `DU` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | **in/out** · Super-diagonal elements (length N-1) |
| ↳ `strideDU` | `integer` | Stride length for `DU` |
| ↳ `offsetDU` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `DU` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × nrhs</sub> | **in/out** · Right hand side matrix (N x nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `B` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrix B. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `DL`: On entry, `DL` must contain the (n-1) sub-diagonal elements of A.

  On exit, `DL` is overwritten by the (n-2) elements of the second super-diagonal of the upper triangular matrix U from the LU factorization of A, in `DL(1)`, ..., `DL(n-2)`.
- `d`: On entry, D must contain the diagonal elements of A.

  On exit, D is overwritten by the n diagonal elements of U.
- `DU`: On entry, `DU` must contain the (n-1) super-diagonal elements of A.

  On exit, `DU` is overwritten by the (n-1) elements of the first super-diagonal of U.
- `B`: On entry, the N by `NRHS` matrix of right hand side matrix B. On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the N by `NRHS` solution matrix X.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, U(i,i) is exactly zero, and the solution has not been computed.  The factorization has not been completed unless $i = N$.

</section>

## Notes

-   `dgtsv()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DGTSV`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dgtsv.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dgtsv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dgtsv';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const B = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const DL = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const d = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const DU = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dgtsv( 'column-major', N, N, DL, 1, d, 1, DU, 1, B, N );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = dgtsv.ndarray( N, N, DL, 1, 0, d, 1, 0, DU, 1, 0, B, N, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DGTSV`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DGTSV solves the equation

$$
A \, X = B
$$

where A is an n by n tridiagonal matrix, by Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting.

Note that the equation $A^T \, X = B$ may be solved by interchanging the order of the arguments `DU` and `DL`.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
